slides.headline: A US visa rejection couldn't stop him. NASA came looking for him instead.
Dr. Anand Megalingam, founder of Space Zone India, was selected for a NASA-linked US State Department leadership programme
slides.body: Born to a tractor driver's family in rural India, he walked nearly six kilometres daily to school, dropped out of college once, then rebuilt his path by shifting from computer science to aeronautical engineering. Years earlier, his US visa application for advanced aerospace research had been rejected.

slides.headline: India's first reusable hybrid rocket, launched from a mobile platform.
slides.body: On August 24, 2024, Space Zone India - founded with his own father as first partner - launched RHUMI-1, India's first reusable hybrid rocket, from a mobile launch pad. The achievement positioned Space Zone India among Asia's emerging private space innovators. In 2026, he was selected among only 23 experts worldwide for a US State Department leadership programme with advanced NASA technical exposure.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: He didn't wait for the door to open. He built one worth knocking on.
slides.body: A Viksit Bharat by 2047 doesn't need permission from anyone else's institution to prove its capability - it needs people who build first, credential later. The visa that was once denied became irrelevant the moment the rocket flew.
